# Oxelis plugins (reference for AI assistants that write plugins)

Oxelis is a screen capture, text recognition and translation tool. Plugins are JavaScript executed in QuickJS, one sandbox per plugin.
A plugin is a folder containing manifest.json and main.js. Start from templates/hello-translate or templates/hello-ml.

Rules:
- main.js is CommonJS: `module.exports = class X { onload(oxelis) { ... } }`. The only global is `oxelis`.
- There is no require, file system, setTimeout, fetch or TextEncoder. Network access is oxelis.http.fetch (blocking) or oxelis.http.fetchAll (parallel, at most 4).
- Network access is https only, restricted to the hosts listed in manifest permissions.net (exact name or "*.suffix") and to the host of a setting named in permissions.netFromSettings. Plain http:// is allowed only to localhost and 127.0.0.1.
- Translators: oxelis.services.translate.register({ id, name, translate(texts, from, to) }). Return an array of strings with the same length as texts. May be async.
- Settings: declare them in the manifest ("settings": [{key, label, secret, default}]) and read them with oxelis.settings.get(key). Secrets must never be written into the plugin. Settings with secret:true are stored encrypted with Windows DPAPI.
- Limits: 48 MB of memory and 60 seconds per call.
- Editor: oxelis.ui.addButton / addPanel / hide, oxelis.theme.set, oxelis.layout.set, oxelis.app.{notify, copy, run, text, translation, selection, lines}, oxelis.on('selection' | 'ocr' | 'translated'). A plugin that extends the editor must list it in the manifest: "provides": ["buttons", "panels", "theme", "layout", "events"]; otherwise it is not started there. Copying to the clipboard requires permissions.clipboard = true.
- The 'ocr' handler receives {lines, source} and may return a new array of lines (post-processing before display).
- Models: permissions.ml = true, then `const m = oxelis.ml.load('models/x.onnx'); m.run({ name: { dtype, shape, data } }, wanted?)` returns { name: { dtype, shape, data } }. At most 8 models; files must be inside the plugin folder; tensors are exchanged as JSON and should be kept small.
- OCR model packs: manifest `ocr: { engine: 'ppocr', det, rec, dict, runtime }`; no main.js is required.
- Credits: a plugin that uses a service, model or program made by others must list it in manifest "credits": [{ name, by, license, url }], with the name spelled as its owner spells it. Models of others are not stored in the repository.
- Registered but not yet invoked by the application: ocr services and commands.
- References: sdk/oxelis.d.ts (types), docs/plugin-api.md (API reference), official/*/main.js (examples).
- Interface languages: manifest `language: { code, name, strings }` plus a catalog file of `key = value` lines (see templates/hello-language); no main.js, no permissions.
- Texts: put user-visible strings in locales/<code>.lang (key = value, {0} {1} placeholders; at least en.lang) and read them with oxelis.t('key', ...args). Never hard-code a language.
